class.name: NetwInterestHandle
class.brief_description: Which layers one entity is in, who may therefore see it, and what it is told when that changes.
class.description:
Membership declarations survive tree exits and reapply when the entity enters a session, so a layer declared in [method Object._init] is the same layer the server admits later. The server owns the real [NetwInterestLayer] membership. Clients keep the same labels and callback surface for local visibility and observer-awareness events. Declaring interest and reading it back are ONE type: [method Netw.configure_interest] returns this handle and so does [member NetwEntity.interest], so a helper takes either and a chain in [method Object._init] is the same object a later frame mutates. Every verb returns the handle, so one chained expression declares an entity's layers and the callbacks that ride them. [codeblock] func _init() -> void: Netw.configure_interest(self) \ .join(&"team:red", NetwMultiplayer.LEAVE_POLICY_RETAIN) \ .join(&"sight") \ .on_enter(_on_interest_enter)
# and the same handle, later: Netw.configure_entity(self).interest.join(&"team:blue") [/codeblock] The handle holds no interest state of its own. Every declaration lives on the entity's own row, which is why a chain declared before the entity attaches to a session is the state the session adopts rather than a copy it has to replay.

method.name: entity
method.description: The [NetwEntity] this handle was bound to, or [code]null[/code] once that entity is gone.

method.name: join
method.description: Adds the entity to [param layer_id] and returns this handle. Idempotent. [param leave_policy] is one of [enum NetwMultiplayer.LeavePolicy] and [param perception_policy] one of [enum NetwMultiplayer.PerceptionPolicy], each declared in passing for the layer being joined. [code]-1[/code] declares neither and leaves whatever [method on_leave_policy] and [method on_perception_policy] already set, which are also the door for the [code]CUSTOM[/code] rows because those need a callback. The declaration is safe in [method Object._init] on every peer. Only server authority mutates the live [NetwInterestLayer] entity set.

method.name: layer_ids
method.description: Returns a copy of the locally known layer labels.

method.name: leave
method.description: Removes the entity from [param layer_id] and returns this handle. Idempotent.

method.name: of
method.description: Ensures the entity rooted at [param node] and returns its [member NetwEntity.interest]. [method Netw.configure_interest] is the front door and this is what it returns. A [param node] that roots no entity is reported and returned [code]null[/code].

method.name: on_enter
method.description: Calls [param callback] with [code](layer_id, peer_id)[/code] whenever this entity becomes visible through [param layer_id], and returns this handle. An empty [param layer_id] registers [param callback] against every layer [method layer_ids] currently returns, which is what lets one chain declare a set of layers and then give them all one callback. It reads what the entity has joined, not what this expression joined, so a callback declared after a later [method join] does not reach back to it.

method.name: on_leave
method.description: Calls [param callback] with [code](layer_id, peer_id)[/code] whenever this entity stops being visible through [param layer_id], and returns this handle. An empty [param layer_id] registers against every layer [method layer_ids] currently returns, as [method on_enter] does.

method.name: on_leave_policy
method.description: Overrides the wire behavior for [param layer_id] with one of [enum NetwMultiplayer.LeavePolicy], and returns this handle. [constant NetwMultiplayer.LEAVE_POLICY_CUSTOM] requires [param custom_callback], called with [code](peer_id, layer_id)[/code] on server authority. Other policies reject a callback so configuration mistakes fail at declaration time.

method.name: on_perception_policy
method.description: Overrides local presentation behavior for [param layer_id] with one of [enum NetwMultiplayer.PerceptionPolicy], and returns this handle. [constant NetwMultiplayer.PERCEPTION_POLICY_CUSTOM] requires [param custom_callback]. The callback receives [code](visible, peer_id, layer_id)[/code] on both local participant edges. Other policies reject a callback.
